title: How the Congo Square dances were run and what music they had
summary: She describes outdoor dances with Creole beer, singing, mule-jaw percussion and spoons, free admission.

blocks.x: I wondered some more about those dances at the Congo Square. How often did they have those? Do you remember?

Oh, well, you see, the colored people would go there whenever they got ready to give their dance. They'd go and put the bière creole, creole bière. They'd make it with the pineapple hull, you know, and the apple. They sell that cider, I believe they call it now.

They'd go at the Congo Square there, and they'd put their little table there, and they'd give you a, settle your glass for a nickel. The nickels wasn't like they are now. The nickels had just like strips like this, and a big five on the other side.
What kind of music did they have for those dances?
Well, sometimes they'd have jabounmule, as they call it. Mule jabounmule.
They use those in Cuba now.

Yeah, yeah. They use them in Cuba. Well, sometimes they'd have them. And if they didn't have that, they'd take tin plates and spoons and make music out of that. But most of the time, it was their mouth. There were the sing. Jolipon. Jolipon Mambo.
Jolipon, Jolipon Mambo. Jolipon Coferto Carré comme ça. Jolipon, ah, Jolipon Mambo. And it keep up with their feet.
Did anybody charge money to get to those dances?
No, no, no money. Anybody could go in there, because many times I got a money beaten for running off to go see those Creole dances at the Congo.
